answer: A sybil attack floods a network with fake agents, so one defense is a cost that scales with identity. Each new agent must spend real verifiable work, like a one-time proof of compute, before it can answer challenges or earn rewards. Picture a lantern at the edge of a fable-like harbor: every boat that wants to dock on the island has to show its stamp first, so a thousand fake boats cost a thousand times the price of one real one.
